headline: Strong US figures, above all a big jump in consumer confidence, lifted the dollar to a near two-week high before Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, while oil slipped as talks with Iran went on.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar rose for a third day to a near two-week high, about 102.3 on the dollar index, after every US figure out today beat forecasts. Consumer confidence jumped the most, a sign households feel better as petrol gets cheaper, the day before the Federal Reserve decides.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation near 3.7%, and markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold rates on Wednesday and raise them in December, which supports the dollar. What changed: Four US reports all came in stronger than expected. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index jumped to 91.7 from 84.2, far above the 81.2 forecast, as falling petrol prices lifted spirits. Orders for long-lasting goods rose 1.8% in September against 0.6% expected; aircraft did much of the work, but orders outside transport still rose 0.5%. New home sales ran at a 676,000 yearly pace, above forecasts, and house prices rose 0.3% in August. The dollar index ended near 102.3, up about 0.3%. Reuters put the odds of a December Fed hike at about 82%. What it means: The US economy is holding up better than feared, and households still expect prices to rise almost 6% over the next year. That gives the Fed less reason to back away from a December hike, and higher expected US rates draw money into the dollar. The question to keep asking: does Fed chair Kevin Warsh keep a December hike clearly on the table?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: The Fed decides at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday, with Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT; a hold is priced at about 90%, so the tone on December matters more than the decision. Before that, US goods trade figures at 7:30 AM CT. US third-quarter growth and the Fed's preferred inflation measure follow on Thursday.
numbers: Dollar index ~102.3 (+0.26%), a near two-week high

scenarios.base: The Fed holds, Warsh keeps December open, and the dollar index stays near 102 to 102.5 into Thursday's growth and inflation figures.
scenarios.bull: Warsh signals a December hike is close to settled, or some officials vote for a hike now; short-term yields rise and the index pushes toward 103.
scenarios.bear: Warsh plays down December, or oil falls further on a deal with Iran; hike bets fade and the index slips back toward 101.7.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro fell for a fifth straight day, to about $1.114, as the dollar firmed and French consumer confidence sank to its lowest since 2013. The European Central Bank decides on Thursday and is expected to hold.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The euro has been weighed down by France's debt and budget fight and by costly imported energy, though a European Central Bank hike in December is widely expected. What changed: France's statistics office said consumer confidence fell to 80 in October, its lowest since June 2013, as protests and money worries hit households. Euro-area money and lending growth held steady, and the vote on France's budget revenues slipped again, to November 3. With strong US figures lifting the dollar, the euro ended near $1.1136, down about 0.3%. What it means: French households are gloomy while American ones are cheering up, and that contrast favours the dollar over the euro. A December ECB hike is still the main support, so the euro leans on what the bank says on Thursday. The question to keep asking: does the ECB stay firm on December despite France's troubles?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Germany's GfK consumer mood survey at 2:00 AM CT Wednesday, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. The ECB decides at 8:15 AM CT Thursday, with President Christine Lagarde's press conference after; euro-area growth figures follow on Friday.
numbers: French consumer confidence (Oct) 80, lowest since June 2013
ECB Oct 29: hold ~93–97%; December hike widely expected

scenarios.base: The euro stays near $1.11 to $1.12 as investors wait for the Fed and the ECB.
scenarios.bull: Lagarde keeps a December hike firmly on the table and French bonds stay calm; the euro climbs back above $1.12.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed and soft ECB tone push the euro toward $1.105, especially if French bond worries return.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound slipped to about $1.331 as the dollar firmed, a day before Chancellor John Healey's first UK Budget. UK shop prices rose at their fastest pace in two and a half years, which keeps a Bank of England hike on November 5 close to certain.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation is running well above target, so markets expect the Bank of England to raise rates on November 5, which supports the pound; the government's borrowing plans are the main worry. What changed: The British Retail Consortium said shop prices rose 2.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 1.4% and above the 1.6% expected, as shops passed on higher energy, transport and wage costs. There was no other UK news. The pound fell about 0.2% to near $1.3310, gaining only against the yen, as investors pulled back bets against the dollar before the Fed. What it means: Rising shop prices back the case for a hike, but the pound is moving with the dollar for now. Reports point to extra investment spending in the Budget; the risk is a bigger jump in borrowing that unsettles UK government bonds. The question to keep asking: does the Budget calm or rattle UK bond markets?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Healey presents the Budget at about 7:30 AM CT Wednesday, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. The Bank of England decides on November 5.
numbers: UK shop prices (Oct) +2.1% y/y vs 1.6% forecast
Bank of England Nov 5: hike to 4.00% ~90–97%

scenarios.base: A Budget with modest extra borrowing leaves the pound between $1.325 and $1.338, moving mostly with the dollar.
scenarios.bull: A Budget that keeps borrowing in check calms UK bonds; the pound recovers toward $1.335 to $1.34.
scenarios.bear: Borrowing well above expectations lifts UK bond yields for the wrong reasons; the pound drops below $1.325.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen weakened again, with the dollar near ¥157.8, as stocks rose and safety demand faded. Japan's finance minister warned the government is ready to act in currency markets, which keeps a lid on how far the dollar can climb.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The yen sits low because Japan's rates are far below other major economies' and the country pays for costly imported energy; a Bank of Japan hike in December is widely expected but not yet signalled. What changed: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama told parliament the government is watching markets with a strong sense of urgency and is ready to take decisive action. Earlier, a Bank of Japan gauge of underlying inflation rose to 3.2%, its highest in three years. Neither moved the yen much; rising stocks and strong US figures lifted the dollar about 0.2% to near ¥157.8. What it means: Inflation in Japan is broadening, which strengthens the case for a December Bank of Japan hike, but that is months away while the rate gap with the US is here now. Katayama's warning matters because the dollar is close to levels where Tokyo has stepped in before. The question to keep asking: how close is Tokyo to buying yen?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday, then Tokyo consumer prices on Wednesday evening, CT. The Bank of Japan decides on Friday, Japan time, with new forecasts; a hold is expected.
numbers: Bank of Japan trend inflation (Sep) 3.2%, a three-year high
Bank of Japan Oct 30: hold ~98%; December hike ~83–88%

scenarios.bull: A firm Fed lifts US yields and pushes the dollar toward ¥158.5, raising the odds that Tokyo acts.
scenarios.bear: A stock sell-off, a softer Fed or action from Tokyo sends the dollar back below ¥157.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc eased, with the dollar up about 0.2% to near 0.829 francs, as rising stocks and strong US figures cut demand for safety. There was no Swiss news.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The franc is pulled between near-zero Swiss inflation, which keeps rates at zero, and its role as a safe place for money when markets are nervous. What changed: With no Swiss data, the franc followed the mood: stocks rose, oil fell and the dollar firmed, so the dollar ended near 0.8289 francs. The Swiss National Bank's next decision is not until December 10, and markets are split on whether it moves. What it means: Calm markets take away the franc's main support, and Swiss rates at zero give investors little reason to hold it. It would firm again quickly if the Iran talks fail or stocks fall. The question to keep asking: are markets nervous enough to seek safety?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: UBS's survey of Swiss economic expectations at 4:00 AM CT Wednesday, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT.

scenarios.base: The dollar stays between 0.825 and 0.833 francs while markets stay calm.
scenarios.bull: A firm Fed and steady stocks lift the dollar toward 0.835 francs.
scenarios.bear: Failed Iran talks or a stock sell-off send money into the franc; the dollar slips below 0.825 francs.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Australian dollar edged up to near 70.3 US cents, holding firm as rising stocks offset a stronger US dollar. Australia's third-quarter inflation figures, due at 7:30 PM CT tonight, will likely decide whether the Reserve Bank of Australia hikes on November 3.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise rates again in November because inflation is running hot, which supports the Aussie, though weak business surveys hold it back. What changed: No Australian news landed during the US session. The Aussie gained about 0.2% to near 0.7028 as stocks rose, one of the few currencies to hold up against the dollar. Markets still put a November hike at about even odds. What it means: Tonight's inflation figures are the turning point. A core reading above what banks expect would make a November hike likely and lift the Aussie; a soft one would push the bank to wait. The question to keep asking: is underlying inflation still too high for the bank?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: a Reserve Bank of Australia appearance before parliament at 7:15 PM CT and the third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT tonight; banks expect core prices up about 1.0% on the quarter. The Fed follows at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday, and the bank decides on November 3.
numbers: Q3 trimmed-mean CPI forecast ~+1.0% q/q (~3.5% y/y)

scenarios.base: Core inflation comes in near 1.0% on the quarter; the Aussie holds between 70 and 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bull: Core inflation above 1.0% makes a November hike likely; the Aussie rises above 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bear: Core inflation at 0.8% or less cools hike bets; the Aussie drops below 70 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie was steady at about 1.403 per US dollar, as falling oil and a firmer US dollar offset each other. The Bank of Canada decides at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday, and a rate hike is mostly expected.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy has pushed Canadian inflation above the Bank of Canada's forecasts, so markets expect a hike this week, which supports the loonie, while US tariffs still weigh on Canada's economy. What changed: There was no Canadian news. US crude slipped back under $100 a barrel, which takes a little away from Canada's oil income, while the US dollar firmed on strong figures. The loonie ended little changed, with the US dollar near 1.4027. What it means: The loonie is waiting on the Bank of Canada. Markets price a hike at about 75–80%, but some big banks expect a hold, so the decision could swing the currency either way. The question to keep asking: does the bank hike and signal more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday, followed by Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. Canada's August growth figures come on Friday.

scenarios.base: The bank hikes as priced; the US dollar holds between 1.398 and 1.407 Canadian.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a signal of more pushes the US dollar below 1.398 Canadian.
scenarios.bear: A hold surprises markets; the US dollar jumps above 1.41 Canadian.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi edged up to near 57 US cents ahead of tonight's Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT, where a rate hike to 3% is widely expected. What the bank says about further hikes matters more than the move itself.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise rates this week because inflation is still above its target band, which has kept the kiwi near the top of the board this month. What changed: No New Zealand news during the US session. The kiwi rose about 0.2% to near 0.5696 as stocks rose, with hike bets for tonight steady at roughly 85–90%. What it means: A hike is mostly priced, so the kiwi's next move rests on the bank's guidance. A signal of more hikes would support it; a hint that this is the last would let it slip. The question to keep asking: does the bank promise more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision and statement at 8:00 PM CT tonight. Australia's inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT come just before it, and the Fed decides at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday.

scenarios.base: A hike to 3% with a steady tone; the kiwi holds near 56.7 to 57.2 cents.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a clear signal of more lifts the kiwi above 57.2 cents.
scenarios.bear: A hike framed as the last, or a surprise hold, sends the kiwi below 56.5 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil gave up a morning bounce and closed lower, with Brent near $115 and US crude just under $100, as talks with Iran continued. A Houthi claim to have hit Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery was not confirmed, and the fire there was put out quickly.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, attacks on Gulf oil sites and shipping near the Strait of Hormuz have kept oil high, which lifts inflation everywhere and helps oil exporters like Canada. What changed: Yemen's Houthis said a missile hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; Saudi Arabia did not confirm it, and a fire near the export terminal was contained within hours. Brent briefly rose above $116, then fell as Iran's supreme leader set conditions for ending the war, which traders read as talking about terms rather than walking away. Iran's navy said a tanker hit a mine east of the strait, but no one else confirmed it. Brent ended near $114.8, down about 0.9%, and US crude near $99.8, down about 2%. UBS raised its year-end Brent forecast to about $110. What it means: Talks are slowly taking some of the war premium out of oil, but attacks keep a floor under it. Cheaper oil eases inflation fears and helps energy importers like Japan and the euro area, while trimming support for the loonie. The question to keep asking: do the talks with Iran produce terms?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US crude stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute at 3:30 PM CT today and the government's figures at 9:30 AM CT Wednesday. Any news from the talks with Iran or new attacks will move prices first.

scenarios.bull: A confirmed hit to Saudi output or a breakdown in talks sends Brent back above $117.
scenarios.bear: Concrete terms from Iran lead to a deal outline; Brent falls toward $108.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold dipped to $4,000 an ounce and bounced, ending little changed near $4,018. Rising odds of a December Fed hike and a firmer dollar weigh on it, but buyers keep stepping in at $4,000.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold hit records earlier this month, then fell about 4% last week as the Federal Reserve signalled more rate rises to fight inflation near 3.7%. What changed: Gold touched $4,000 early on Tuesday as the dollar firmed, then recovered as buyers stepped in. Strong US figures kept bets on a December Fed hike high, at about 82% in a Reuters reading. Gold ended near $4,018, about flat. What it means: Higher expected US rates make a metal that pays no interest less attractive and push the dollar up, which weighs on gold. Its war-time safety appeal is fading a little as talks with Iran go on. The question to keep asking: does the Fed sound firm enough on December to break $4,000?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT, then US third-quarter growth and the Fed's preferred inflation measure on Thursday.

scenarios.base: The Fed holds with December open; gold stays between $3,960 and $4,080.
scenarios.bull: Warsh sounds cautious on December, or Iran talks fail; gold rises above $4,080.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed signal on December breaks $4,000 and sends gold toward $3,950.

calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
